text:
Alexander Wennberg has played only 14 of San Jose's games, in and out of the lineup through October and November, and he scored his first goal of the season this month, "off the slump and on the board," as Max Miller put it. Four points in 14 games is a long way from last season's 55, though he's right back in the middle of things at 20:29 a night.

Our numbers read the slump as mostly luck so far. He has one goal on 2.9 expected, and his point rate (0.84 per 60) sits far below his talent range of roughly 1.5 to 2.2. That gap tends to close. The five-on-five numbers are poor (43% of the expected goals with him on), but that's partly the Sharks, who lose the chance battle most nights. He carries the puck in on 60% of his entries in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and Evolving-Hockey liked his defense last season. Our range projects 31 to 51 points. He just needs to stay in the lineup.
